crossModelInterpretation: The frozen raw owner-native packets were already sufficient for both models in this task-selection suite; no wrapper has earned default insertion merely by matching raw correctness.

P0/P3 preserved correctness but added about 3.06x caller prompt bytes and about 55-57% mean Provider token use in both models; retain them for ambiguity/cross-owner diagnostics rather than automatic wrapping of clear owner surfaces.

P1's exact reusable-source mechanism remains valid, but task-fit selection is semantic authority: Flash showed negative transfer from a deliberately generic procedure while Pro did not. This reinforces explicit selection and rejects automatic/default reusable-procedure injection.
Full bundling did not dominate the simpler baseline: Flash was 19/20 versus raw 20/20 and Pro was tied 8/8 with materially higher token use.
Model robustness can mask interface/procedure mismatch; the weaker Flash primary is useful for exposing substrate-consumption friction that Pro can compensate for.
